CweFindings.Name: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition
CweFindings.Description: The product does not properly check inputs that are used for loop conditions, potentially leading to a denial of service or other consequences because of excessive looping.
CweFindings.Explanation: HomeController.uploadPhotos loops over the entire caller-supplied multipart files list (68-91), invoking upload parsing and database writes for each item, without checking a maximum count. The configured max-files-per-upload value is never injected or consulted. Authenticated callers can submit many small files and induce repeated ImageIO and repository work. The 50MB request limit bounds total request bytes, but does not enforce the intended ten-file processing budget; parser-specific part-count limits may further bound exposure and were not validated.

CweFindings.Name: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value
CweFindings.Description: The product allocates memory based on an untrusted, large size value, but it does not ensure that the size is within expected limits, allowing arbitrary amounts of memory to be allocated.
CweFindings.Explanation: An anonymous GET / calls HomeController.index -> PhotoServiceImpl.getAllPhotos -> PhotoRepository.findAllOrderByUploadedAtDesc. The unpaginated query selects PHOTO_DATA for every persisted row (22-27), materializing all BLOB byte arrays and entities even though the page needs metadata only. Total allocation scales with the uploaded dataset without an aggregate bound; repeated requests can exhaust the configured 512MB heap. Authenticated uploads can grow the dataset; no particular current database size or successful denial of service is asserted.

CweFindings.Name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
CweFindings.Description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.
CweFindings.Explanation: azure-setup.ps1 stores the generated database password ([MASKED]) in the project .env via Out-File (299), without setting a restrictive Unix mode/umask or Windows ACL before or after creation. On a shared Unix host with the common 022 umask, a newly created file is readable by other local users, exposing application database credentials. This is a conditional deployment-script permission finding, not a claim that the current host has executed the script or that an existing .env currently has weak permissions. Git ignore does not restrict local file access.

CweFindings.Name: Insufficient Logging
CweFindings.Description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.
CweFindings.Explanation: The authenticated destructive DetailController.deletePhoto action logs the target photo ID and outcome (69), and PhotoServiceImpl.deletePhoto similarly logs only the target ID (212). Neither records the acting authenticated principal, source or an audit correlation identity. Consequently these security-critical mutation records do not identify the actor. SecurityConfig uses HTTP Basic without an application audit handler; external proxy/SIEM audit coverage is unknown. Operational logging exists, but relevant audit details are omitted.

CweFindings.Name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
CweFindings.Description: The product allows the upload or transfer of dangerous file types that are automatically processed within its environment.
CweFindings.Explanation: PhotoServiceImpl.uploadPhoto trusts the multipart Content-Type allowlist (88), but a header-spoofed non-image with no ImageIO reader is not rejected (130-149) and is saved unchanged (160-174). Arbitrary unrecognized content can therefore be persisted and publicly served by PhotoFileController.servePhoto (75-83). Upload requires authenticated credentials. File extension is also unvalidated; no server-side script execution or browser MIME bypass is established.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
CweFindings.Description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.
CweFindings.Explanation: upload.js handleFiles includes an untrusted local or dropped file name in validation error messages (73-82). showErrors interpolates each message into an li and assigns innerHTML (216-218), allowing filename markup to become active HTML in the uploader browser. No authentication or server response is needed for this client-side error path. This is a DOM XSS sink; victim interaction with a specially named file is required. The successful upload response also reaches unescaped originalFileName interpolation in createPhotoCard (185-189) and insertAdjacentHTML (157); server-rendered Thymeleaf th:text paths escape names.
